description:
About the Position

The Stockholm Resilience Centre invites applications for a PhD student position in sustainability science. The Centre, part of Stockholm University's Faculty of Science, is internationally known for research on resilience thinking, planetary boundaries and the governance of social-ecological systems. Doctoral researchers at the Centre work on questions of how ecosystems and societies interact across scales - from local resource management to global sustainability governance - combining natural and social science methods in applied, solution-oriented projects.

The position is a salaried four-year doctoral employment under the Swedish collective agreement. Candidates join an interdisciplinary supervisor team and a centre with dense international networks among sustainability researchers, funders and practitioners. The working language is English, and the Centre's doctoral programme includes coursework in sustainability science methods, systems thinking and stakeholder engagement, with fieldwork components shaped by the chosen project.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in sustainability science, environmental science, geography, ecology or a related interdisciplinary field, and show the ability to work across natural and social science approaches. Experience with systems analysis, modelling or qualitative fieldwork is an advantage depending on the project line. Applications are submitted through Stockholm University's Varbi system with CV, degree certificates, references and a motivation letter describing the applicant's research interests in resilience and sustainability.

Highlights

  • PhD in sustainability science at the Stockholm Resilience Centre
  • World-leading resilience and planetary boundaries research
  • Interdisciplinary social-ecological systems approach
  • Salaried four-year employment per Swedish collective agreement
  • International networks and solution-oriented projects
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

About Stockholm University

Stockholm University is a public research university in the Swedish capital with roughly 30,000 students and a strong research profile in the natural sciences, psychology, humanities, law and social sciences. Many of its departments collaborate with national research institutes located on the same campus areas, including the neighbouring Science for Life Laboratory environment. Doctoral students in Sweden are employed on paid contracts with collective-agreement salaries and full social benefits. PhD and postdoctoral vacancies are recruited through the national Varbi system used by Swedish universities.
